newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Rate on Yugo c.bank bonds falls to 58.69 pct.
newsitem.headline: Rate on Yugo c.bank bonds falls to 58.69 pct.

text.p: The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) sharply cut an interest rate on its short-term bonds auctioned on Friday to an annual 58.69 percent, the Belgrade bourse reported.
This compares to an annual 88.89 percent set for its previous tranche of bonds auctioned February 12.

"The rate on those bonds had to go down following the latest cut in the NBY discount rate to 2.5 from 4.5 percent per month, and based on the low 0.6 percent February inflation," head of the NBY Department for Open Market Operations Voja Scekic told Reuters.
The new tranche of bonds carried a four percent monthly rate.
The NBY offered for sale a new 20-million dinar ($3.58 million) tranche of its 30-day bonds, maturing April 13, but sold only 0.3 million dinars worth, said the bourse spokesman Milko Stimac.
Traders said demand would have been greater if the central bank had made its 15 percent reserve requirement clearer.
According to the latest NBY decision, banks fulfil the reserve requirment by transferring 15 percent of their deposits, but also by depositing with the NBY 15 percent of money lent to other banks.
Unclear technicalities over whether activity between commercial banks and the central bank was also treated as interbank activity, kept investors away during the auction.

"There is no official explanation, and banks have to deposit 15 percent with the NBY when purchasing other commercial banks' bonds. It would be too much to buy NBY bonds and to pay 15 percent reserve requirement on top of it," a trader said.
The NBY will publish additional interpretation of its latest reserve requirement decision next week, a central bank senior official said.
"But the 15 percent reserve requirement does not refer to the NBY bonds," the source said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
